vo: Free AI note takers aren't free in the same way.
One caps your minutes, one caps your meetings, one caps the AI.
Here's the fine print, side by side.
We'll cover the three kinds of free limits, how the big plans compare, and at the end, the three signs it's actually time to pay.
This is the Lynkk channel, and yes, Lynkk has a free plan too, so we'll put ours in the same table as everyone else's.
Every free plan limits you in one of three ways: total minutes per month, length or number of meetings, or how much AI you get on top of the recording.
Knowing which limit you'll hit first is the whole game.

head: Minute caps.
Fine for a few calls.
scenes.body: Otter's free plan works this way.

card.title: Free plan
card.label: Minutes used this month
card.result: Compare this number with the cap.

vo: Monthly minute caps.
Some tools give you a bucket of minutes each month.
Otter's free plan works this way.
It's great if you have a few short calls a week.
But if you're in back-to-back meetings, you can burn through the bucket in a few days, and then you're back to typing.
Ask yourself: how many hours of meetings do you have in a normal week?
Multiply by four.
That's the number to compare against.

head: Length and count caps.
Watch the long demos.
scenes.body: Granola's free tier covers a limited number of meetings.

card.title: Demo call · Recording
card.cut: Buyer: "So our budget for this is..."

vo: Meeting-length and meeting-count caps.
Other tools let you record as often as you want, but cap how long each meeting can be, or how many meetings you get.
Granola's free tier, for example, covers a limited number of meetings.
Length caps are sneaky.
A 30-minute cap sounds fine until your demo runs long, and the recording stops right when the buyer starts talking about budget.

head: AI caps.
A transcript isn't notes.
scenes.body: Fathom: unlimited recordings, with some advanced AI held back for paid plans.

vo: AI summary caps.
The third type records everything but limits the smart part: the summaries, the action items, the questions you can ask.
Fathom is known for a generous free plan with unlimited recordings, with some of the advanced AI features held back for paid plans.
This matters because a transcript alone isn't notes.
If you have to read a 40-minute transcript to find the next step, you haven't saved much time.

it's time to pay.

scenes.body: None of these? Stay free. Use one plan every day for two weeks first.
vo: So when is paying worth it?
Three signs.
One: you hit your cap before the month is half over.
Two: you're spending time reading transcripts because the AI part ran out.
Three: you need features free plans rarely include, like asking questions across all your past calls.
On Lynkk, that's Ask Lynkk, and it's a Pro feature.
If none of those apply, stay free.
Seriously.
Pick the free plan whose limit you're least likely to hit, and use it every day for two weeks before paying for anything.
